$$\begin{aligned}
|I|-|N_H(I)|
&\ge |X\setminus N_H(X)|-|N_H(X)\setminus X|\\

\end{aligned}$$

$$|N_A(x)|\ge 2,$$

$$N_{S\setminus\{s\}}(x)=\{\tau(x)\},
\qquad

Earlier results and the colouring reductionsLemma 1For arbitrary  $X\subseteq V(H)$ , put  $I=X\setminus N_H(X)$ . Then  $I$  is independent and
$$N_H(I)\subseteq N_H(X)\setminus X.$$
Therefore
$$|I|-|N_H(I)|
\ge |X\setminus N_H(X)|-|N_H(X)\setminus X|
=|X|-|N_H(X)|.$$
This proves equality of the independent and unrestricted deficiency maxima. Hall deficiency on the left side of  $D(H)$  then gives
$$\delta(H)=n-\nu(D(H)).$$
The fractional-matching identity is also correct. A matching in  $D(H)$  contributes half a unit to each corresponding base-edge occurrence, producing a feasible fractional matching of half its cardinality. Conversely, duplicating a fractional base-edge weight onto the two directed copies gives a bipartite fractional matching of twice the total weight. Bipartite integrality supplies
$$\nu(D(H))=2\nu_f(H).$$
Theorem 2The TP-to-PZ injection is valid. In a TP rung, let  $t\in T$ ,  $p=\tau(t)\in P$ , and let  $q$  be the actual mate of  $p$ . Symmetry gives  $t\sim\tau(q)$ . This neighbour is distinct from  $p$ , because  $q\ne t$ . Since  $p$  already uses the one allowed neighbour of  $t$  in  $T\cup P$ , feasibility forces  $\tau(q)\in Z$ .Thus  $q$ 's rung is PZ. Its unique  $P$ -endpoint and that endpoint’s unique actual mate recover the source, proving injectivity.The TT indices are independent, and their entire base neighbourhood consists of ZZ rungs. These facts prove the representative upper bound. The dissociation construction supplies the matching lower bound.Direct colouring reductionsThe required convention is the standard sub-quorum one: a partial colouring, with the quorum measured in each coloured vertex’s coloured closed neighbourhood. Sahbi’s definition explicitly uses this convention. arxiv.orgUnder that convention, both direct reductions are sound:Assigning distinct colours to a dissociation set works because each coloured closed neighbourhood contains at most two vertices, including the vertex itself.From a colour class containing an edge, retain one such edge. From an independent colour class, retain one vertex  $t$ . The latter originally has only itself as a same-colour vertex in its closed neighbourhood, so the quorum condition permits at most one other coloured neighbour. Restricting to the retained support preserves that bound.The retained edges are vertex-disjoint because they come from distinct colour classes. They and the retained singleton representatives form the required feasible pair, with one objective contribution per colour.For complete self-containment, an explicit definition sentence for  $\psi_{\rm sq}$  would improve the note. This is a presentation improvement, not a repair to the reductions.Theorem 3The simultaneous swaps are disjoint for the stated reasons:A bad rung has its white endpoint in  $T\subseteq Q$ .Its mate rung has its white endpoint in  $P$ .Therefore a mate index cannot also be a bad index.Distinct bad black endpoints have distinct actual white mates.Feasibility forces the swapped-in black partner of each selected white vertex to lie in  $Q$ . An untouched selected white vertex retains its black  $Q$  rung partner.Every selected terminal consequently lies on a one-edge auxiliary terminal path containing no actual edge. Its expense is zero for every allowed nonnegative weight assignment. The tagged-union treatment of common actual and auxiliary edges as terminal-free cycles is consistent.Empty actual matchings, perfect actual matchings, empty selections, and zero weights introduce no exception.5. Cartesian prisms and edge casesFor bipartite  $H$ , exchange the layer-to-colour assignment on one class of a base bipartition. This gives
$$E(H)\cong H\square K_2.$$
Also,  $D(H)$  is the disjoint union of two copies of  $H$ , so
$$\nu(D(H))=2\nu(H).$$
Kőnig’s theorem then yields
$$2n-\nu(D(H))
=2(n-\nu(H))
=2\alpha(H).$$
Thus Corollary 5 follows exactly as stated. Bipartiteness is essential to this identification and is correctly retained.The ten-vertex example follows for the stated bipartite gap block: bipartiteness gives  $\alpha(B)\ge5$ , while  $\alpha(B)\le\beta_2(B)=5$ , hence its prism value is ten.The relevant boundary cases are consistent:CaseCheck $n=0$ The empty set is inclusion-minimal forming; all values are zero.Edgeless  $H$  $E(H)=nK_2$ . Implementation and standalone-checker auditI found no substantive implementation defect in the attached versions.The main points supporting that assessment are:Matching construction: optimum_certificate uses iterative augmenting paths. The parent pointers and alternating-path reversal maintain a genuine matching. Alternating reachability produces the Hall set and equal-size vertex cover.Independent optimality certificate: check_certificate verifies a genuine matching and a vertex cover of the same cardinality. This certifies maximum matching cardinality independently of the augmenting-path implementation.Literal formation: minimal_forming_certificate tests the original formation predicate and every single deletion before asserting structural consequences. It does not infer minimality from the claimed optimum.Correct budget representation: Each empty-rung budget is a set of deleted vertices. If both lifts witness the same deletion, it is counted once within that rung; overlaps between different rungs remain visible.Independent exhaustive calculation: literal_optima computes formation and dissociation directly from adjacency bit masks. Its single-deletion lookup is valid because deleting a set bit always produces a smaller mask, already processed.Representative enumeration: pair_controls enumerates actual matchings and all disjoint selected subsets, testing feasibility directly.Alternating-path scoring: score walks the physical auxiliary/actual paths and accumulates actual-edge weights. It includes zero and very large integer weights.Empty graph execution: The expressions involving % n occur only in loops that are empty when  $n=0$ , so there is no zero-modulus defect.One coverage distinction matters: white_subsets_certified counts subsets covered by a construction, not separate calls for every subset. For each actual matching, the checker constructs a completion for the maximal admissible white set. That same completion directly pairs every subset of those selected vertices, so the reported coverage is justified.7.
